title: Superbot size is set by bot number and fusion requires exposed basal layers

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Superbot size is set by bot number and fusion requires exposed basal layers

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Anthrobots fuse into larger superbots only in the days immediately after release from the matrix, while their basal layers are still exposed and can mediate bot-to-bot fusion, and superbot size can be controlled by the number of Anthrobots cultured together in a well.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The tendency of the bots to fuse together and thus form different sized collectives (i.e., superbots) for different scratches can be controlled by modulating the number of Anthrobots cultured together in the same well for fusion, which happens only on days immediately following dissolution while the Anthrobot basal layers are still exposed and thus can mediate the bot‐to‐bot fusion.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Discussion”. Scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots in the days after matrix dissolution

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-25: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.60

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Bot count, fusion timing, size, and polarity are measurable variables. Existing observations can test early fusion qualitatively, but they do not fully establish controllability or the proposed basal-layer mechanism.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Model final superbot size against starting bot number and fusion day, and correlate fusion success with measured basal-surface exposure.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Systematic starting-number and fusion-time series may not be public.

Basal exposure may be inferred rather than measured during each fusion event.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.6
analysis feasibility: 0.72
data adequacy: 0.34
data existence: 0.48
operationalizability: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Superbot size versus the number of input bots, and fusion versus basal-surface exposure, are both countable. The paper describes the control and the time window without releasing the counts or a basal-marker time series. Timing after dissolution is not itself a measurement of exposed basal layers, so the mechanism clause needs data that are not public.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Vary the number of bots per well in the days after matrix release and measure superbot size, and compare fusion rates while a basal marker is still on the surface versus after the surface is apical. Size scaling with bot number, and fusion restricted to the basal-exposed window, would support both clauses; size independent of number, or fusion after basal markers are covered, would refute them.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Basal exposure is inferred from time since dissolution rather than from a paired basal-marker series.

Well crowding can change fusion without any special role for the basal surface.

Fusion counts versus bot number are not deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.38
data existence: 0.16
operationalizability: 0.78
analysis feasibility: 0.18
data adequacy: 0.14
